title: Reindexing, K-injectives and normalized total limit on integral towers
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $b,o,q$ be the specified strict-tower operations and coordinates. Let $g_X:X'\to X$, $g_Y:Y'\to Y$, $f:X\to Y$ and $f':X'\to Y'$ be a Cartesian scheme square with a compactification $c$ of $f$ and its prescribed Cartesian pullback. Assume $\ell$ is invertible in every residue field at all four vertices and both vertical maps are quasi-compact. Fix tower adjunction data $a$ and compatible integral data $s$, including the four normalized reduction/limit coordinates, actual support and right-adjoint comparisons, and their counit and pullback normalization equations. These are the data and functors of [def-pur-integral-geometric-comparison-data, det-sp-tower-exceptional-bc]. If both horizontal maps are scheme isomorphisms, ReindexingPart is nonempty: the completed reindexing predicates (including exact equivalences on completed modules and fixed-ring towers) hold, the actual varying-ring inverse images preserve K-injectives, and pullback commutes with the normalized total limits with precisely the two reconstruction-unit equations. This asserts no smooth purity or support exchange.

proof.text:
use the coefficient isomorphism compatible with every quotient projection to
identify ordinary inverse image with exact reindexing on completed modules and fixed-ring
and varying-ring strict towers. Its exact inverse is inverse reindexing. Transpose a map
from an acyclic complex through this equivalence. The inverse preserves acyclicity, so
K-injectivity supplies a null homotopy, which transposes back. This proves the three
K-injective assertions, without claiming evaluation preserves K-injectives. Apply ordinary
inverse-limit commutation to a K-injective resolution after scalar restriction. This gives
the derived limit comparison. The reconstruction units and the projection normalization
of the reindexing comparison give exactly PullLimit.unit. For ell-power rather than
uniformizer-power indices, write ell as a unit times a positive power of the uniformizer
and apply cofinal Roos restriction; its maps preserve quotient augmentations. Exact
countable products and the strict Roos/derived-limit comparison justify this restriction.
The argument applies to each horizontal isomorphism separately, including identities.
